title: Kenyan Coconut Celebration Dessert
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Coconut Celebration Dessert — a layered dessert of coconut panna cotta, mango coulis, toasted coconut, and passion fruit, served in individual glasses. The showpiece coastal celebration dessert — visually stunning and perfectly aligned with the tropical flavours of the Kenyan coast.
longDesc: The coconut celebration dessert is what coastal Kenyan hospitality looks like in dessert form — layered in individual glasses, glistening with coconut panna cotta, golden with mango coulis, and topped with toasted coconut and the dramatic seeds of fresh passion fruit. It is both beautiful to look at and extraordinary to eat.
ingredients: 2½ tsp agar agar powder (vegetarian) or 2½ tsp gelatin
3 large ripe mangoes — peeled and blended
steps: Make panna cotta: heat coconut milk with sugar, vanilla, and rose water until nearly boiling.
Dissolve agar agar in 4 tbsp cold water, then whisk into hot coconut milk.
Pour into glasses, filling each halfway. Refrigerate until set — 2 hours.
Make mango coulis: blend mango with sugar and lime until smooth. Strain.
Once panna cotta is set, spoon mango coulis on top of each glass.
Just before serving, add a passion fruit half on top of each glass.
chefTips: Agar agar sets firmer and faster than gelatin and is vegan — a good choice for this recipe.
The rose water is subtle but adds the coastal celebratory character.
Make 24 hours ahead for the best set.
commonMistakes: Not allowing the panna cotta to fully set before adding the mango layer.
Over-sweetening the coulis — the mango should be bright and tart.
cookingScience: Agar agar is a polysaccharide derived from seaweed that gels at around 40°C — significantly higher than the body temperature at which gelatin gels would melt. This makes agar-set desserts more stable in Kenyan heat conditions.
sustainabilityTips: Agar agar is plant-based and sustainable — preferable to animal gelatin for this dessert.
healthBenefits: Mango adds vitamin C and A.
culturalNote: The coconut celebration dessert represents the modern face of Swahili coastal hospitality — taking the traditional coastal ingredients of coconut, mango, and passion fruit and presenting them with a elegance that honours both the tradition and the occasion.
